// 01 — About

Who I Am

I'm a Mechanical Engineering master's student at Southern University, currently working in robotics manufacturing while finishing my degree. My day-to-day involves hands-on electromechanical assembly, subsystem testing, and working alongside manufacturing engineers on production-line improvements for autonomous robotic systems.

I am here to build things. Physical things, well-made things, things that actually work.

That production experience has changed how I think about hardware. I care about how parts fit together, how tolerances affect real assemblies, and what happens when a design meets the bench. I use SolidWorks and ANSYS for CAD and simulation work, and I have built full assemblies and part libraries covering robotic arms, mechanical systems, and machine components.

I want to get upstream of production: designing parts and sub-assemblies, building and breaking prototypes fast, thinking through DFM and manufacturing constraints early, and collaborating across mechanical, electrical, and firmware teams. That is the work I am aiming for.

I also carry a research background, maintaining a 4.0 GPA while running ML models for materials prediction under an NSF-funded initiative. That work has made me rigorous about documentation, testing, and cross-functional communication. I have presented at SPE ANTEC 2026 and NSBE 2026, mentored undergraduates, and led team meetings. I work well across disciplines and I am used to environments where things are still being figured out.
